verdicts.note: The only cited evidence is the pamphlet's list of accomplishments ('historic K-12 and affordable housing investments', expanded childcare, free college for low-income families) [S1]. That is the same kind of evidence scored +1 medium for Leavitt and Bronoske in LD28; the dossier has no budget vote or statement that puts investment ahead of restraint as the main lever. Tax votes belong on the taxes axis.

The 'transform our policing systems' language comes from an undated site from about 2020-2021 [S2][S3]; the 2026 pamphlet only cites safety improvements and gun-violence reduction [S1]. +1 medium holds; do not raise it.

Checked rollcalls-1296.xml: besides yea on House third reading (2025-03-12) and final passage as amended by the Senate (2025-04-24), Jinkins voted nay on all ten contested Republican floor amendments roll-called on 2025-03-12 that would have added to the I-2081 rights list (e.g. Burnett 382, monthly evening/weekend curriculum review; 39-42 yeas each), and yea only on two near-unanimous ones (Couture 428, immediate notification of alleged staff sexual misconduct, 93-0; Barkis 462, right to request charter-school enrollment, 92-1). That is not a mixed record: every split vote went toward school discretion, and the two consensus yeas only argue against +2, which was not given. +1 high stands on recorded votes. The dossier should add the amendment votes under Parents and schools.
'No Income tax' is a direct stance against the pole_b flagship (ESSB 6346 context). One terse statement, so medium rather than high.
'Balance the budget yearly', framed as upholding the constitution [S1]; restraint direction, low magnitude. -1 medium holds.
'Support our Law enforcement and tough on crime' plus anti-cartel trafficking [S1]: explicit enforcement framing. Medium (pamphlet only) is the right confidence.

Pamphlet-only, but the statement is explicit and sex-based across three settings (restrooms, sports, prisons) [S1]. Other Pierce/King scorings give similarly explicit sex-based sports/locker-room statements -2 medium and the vaguer 'protect girls' sports' slogan -1 medium. Nothing on abortion keeps it at medium.

'Support Parents Rights' is a slogan with no specifics [S1]. -1 (not -2) already reflects that, and it matches the -1 medium given to the comparable 'protect girls' sports' slogan on social. Medium is the ceiling.
